title: Distributed Stream Scenario Orchestrator for large-scale SSE/WebSocket chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a production-faithful, distributed load harness that exercises streaming chat/completions over both SSE and WebSocket at scale and surfaces tokens/sec, p95 tail latency, and automated regression detection. Scope includes multi-region orchestration (us-west/us-east/eu), synthetic user profiles (short/long prompts, multi-turn), KV-cache warmup sequences, connection churn patterns, and backend failure injection (10% transient errors, 5% slow responses). The orchestrator will: 1) provision lightweight clients across k8s jobs and cloud VMs, 2) maintain tens of thousands of concurrent streaming connections, 3) emit per-request metrics (tokens_sent, tokens_received, token_rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, bytes/sec) to Prometheus, 4) store raw event traces and transcripts to S3 for deterministic replay, and 5) run regression detection (CUSUM + bootstrap) comparing current runs to baseline windows and raise alerts when p95 increases by configurable deltas. Trade-offs: we prioritize fidelity (accurate streaming behavior, KV-cache effects, backpressure) over synthetic throughput-only tests; this increases cost and complexity but yields actionable regressions. Implementation notes: custom Go-based streaming driver (reason: k6 doesn't natively support long-lived streaming with incremental token-level metrics), light-weight orchestrator in Rust for connection fanout, and a control plane that schedules scenarios, rotates prompt seeds, and collates results. Deliverables: harness code, Grafana dashboards, automated CI job, runbook, and a public experiment comparing SSE vs WS for our runtime under identical payload distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can sustain 50k concurrent streaming clients (mixed SSE and WebSocket) across 2 regions without client OOM
Per-route metrics (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, connection success rate) are emitted to Prometheus and visible in Grafana
Automated regression detection flags p95 regressions using CUSUM with configurable sensitivity and archives flagged run artifacts to S3
Baseline vs candidate comparison pipeline produces an HTML summary report and diffs for token-level output quality regressions
CI integration: nightly benchmark job runs and archives metrics; failing regression gates create a blocking build annotation/pager signal
comments: 2026-03-02: PoC completed — small cluster (2000 connections) using Go driver. Observed correct incremental token telemetry; CUSUM prototype implemented in Python.
2026-03-05: Switched from k6 to custom Go driver because k6 lacks stable per-token streaming hooks. Initial Rust orchestrator scaffolded for fanout control plane (see design doc).

2026-03-09: First 10k concurrent streaming run across us-west + eu completed. Measured tokens/sec baseline and saw expected KV warmup effects (first 2 prompts ~30% slower). Logged artifacts to s3://benchmarks/eng-20347/2026-03-09-run1/

2026-03-11: Regression detected during canary against runtime-2.3: p95 increased by 18% on long-turn conversations when batch size > 8. Investigating kernel selection changes from last deploy. Assigned ENG-20600 to narrow CPU vs CUDA kernel impact.
2026-03-12: Design review feedback from PM (Jules Nguyen) to add deterministic replay seeds and redact PII in saved transcripts. Added retention policy for raw traces (30 days).
2026-03-14: Opened PR #1203 with harness + Prometheus exporters. Requesting review from runtime-team and observability (cc @Diego, @Maya Rao). Next: add SLO gating and wire CI nightly job.
